messages.subject: hyperparameter or fixed effect
parts:
Let the model with linear predictor
      \alpha_j + s_i*\beta_j,   s_i is a latent model.
I use INLA to fit \beta_j using copy strategy.
But I have an expressive number of \beta_j.
It is possible to fit \beta_j such as fixed effect?
Or another latent model?

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] hyperparameter or fixed effect
parts:
On Fri, 2012-07-27 at 07:10 -0700, Elias T. Krainski wrote:
> Let the model with linear predictor
> \alpha_j + s_i*\beta_j, s_i is a latent model.
> I use INLA to fit \beta_j using copy strategy.
> But I have an expressive number of \beta_j.
> It is possible to fit \beta_j such as fixed effect?
> Or another latent model?

would it be better if you could express the linear predictor as

A %*% a + S %*% s

where 'a' and 's' are vectors of fixed effects, and A and S two
matrices ?

INLA support this format,

formula = y ~ -1 + A + S

where A and S are matrices.

would this help?

the names of the fixed effects are taken from the appropriate names of
the matrices, with the variable name as the prefix.

here is a small example:

n = 100

n.a = 3
A = matrix(runif(n*n.a), n, n.a)
a = rnorm(n.a)

n.s = 5
S = matrix(runif(n*n.s), n, n.s)
s = rnorm(n.s)

y = 0 + A %*% a + S %*% s + rnorm(n, sd = 0.01)
formula = y ~ -1 + A + S
r = inla(formula, data = list(y=y, A=A, S=S))
summary(r)

print(paste("error", sum(abs(r$summary.fixed[,"mean"] -
c(a,s)))))


--

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] hyperparameter or fixed effect
parts:
I have a latent model z. It is replicated m times multiplied by constant b[j], j=1, 2, ..., m. So, variance of z changes m times. I think that b[j] can be estimated using copy strategy.

Let me clarify with an example:

n <- 100; m <- 5
a <- 3*(m:1/m); b <- 1:m/m

j <- rep(1:m, each=n)
x <- rep(rnorm(n), m)*b[j]
y <- rpois(n*m, exp(a[j] + x))

tapply(x, b[j], sd)
tapply(y, a[j], mean)

formula <- update(y ~ 0 + j + f(i, wi, model="iid", initial=0, fixed=TRUE),
                  paste(".~.+", paste('f(i.',1:m,', w.',1:m,
                                      ", copy='i', fixed=FALSE)",
                                      sep="", collapse="+")))

dat <- data.frame(y=y, j=factor(j), i=rep(1:n,m), wi=rep(0,n*m),
                  i=kronecker(matrix(1,m,m), 1:n),
                  w=kronecker(diag(m),rep(1,n)))

require(INLA)
res <- inla(formula, data=dat, family="poisson")
cbind(true=a, res$summary.fix)
cbind(true=b, res$summary.hyperpar)

It is possible to fit b[j] without specify it such as hyperparameter?

All the best!
Elias T. Krainski

aaah, now I see. it seems to me that this is the way to doit. as you
have a term 'beta*x', where both are random, you need to condition on
one of them to have a latent Gaussian model, ie you'll need to put one
of them into the hyperparameters.
